We need to find airport codes that satisfy certain conditions:

- Use BTS Average Domestic Airline Itinerary Fares 2020 dataset – presumably for each quarter. For 2020, we have Q1 and Q2 average fares by airport codes.
- Determine airports where average fare in Q2 > Q1.
- Among those, pick airports with at least 4 other airports in the same state. So the airport's state must have at least 5 airports total including that airport.
- The airport code (typically IATA code like LAX) must start with a different letter than the listing city name's starting letter. # Average Air Fares Dropped to All-Time Low in 2020

 Tuesday, April 20, 2021

**Release Number:**BTS 27-21

![Image 5](https://www.bts.gov/sites/bts.dot.gov/files/images/Air%20Fare%20Infographic%204Q2020.png)

The 2020 average domestic itinerary air fare of $292 was the lowest inflation-adjusted annual fare since the Bureau of Transportation Statistics began collecting such records in 1995, down 19% from the previous low of $359 in 2019.

In 2020, 131 million originating passengers traveled on U.S. airlines, down from 331 million in 2019.

During the year, fares dropped in the third quarter to $245, inflation-adjusted, the lowest quarterly fare on record. In the fourth quarter, fares rose to $261, up 6% from the third quarter but down 28% from the fourth quarter 2019 average fare of $361.

**Annual Air Fares**

**Inflation-adjusted**

Annual 2020 fare: $292

From Previous Year: Down 18.6% from 2019 ($359)

All Years: Down 42.6% from the highest fare for any year, $510 in 2000

Start of BTS records in 1995: Down 41.1% from 1995 ($496)

Recent high: Down 31.7% from 2014 ($428)

**Unadjusted**

Annual 2020 fare: $292

From Previous Year: Down 17.6% from 2019 ($355)

All Years: Down 25.4% from the highest fare for any year, $392 in 2014

Start of BTS records in 1995: Up .06% ($292) (compared to 69.8% consumer price index increase)

Recent low: Down 5.8% from 2009 ($310)

**Fare calculations by BTS**

**Itinerary Fares**_:_ Round-trips, but includes one-ways if no return is purchased.

Breakout of trip types:one-way, 42% ($222); round-trip: 58%, ($358).

Based on a random sample of 10% of the tickets.

**Total ticket value:** The price charged by airlines at time of ticket purchase.

**Included:**Additional taxes and fees levied by an outside entity at time of ticket purchase.

**Not included:** Fees for optional services, such as baggage fees.

**Other Revenue:** In recent years, airlines have increasingly obtained additional revenue from passenger fees, as well as from other sources. U.S. passenger airlines collected 65.1% of total operating revenue of $38.6 billion from passenger fares during the first nine months of 2020, down from 88.5% in 1990 _._

Results for average fares are based on the BTS Origin & Destination Survey, a 10% sample of airline tickets used during the quarter _._ For results based on all itinerary fares for 2020, the standard error is 0.18. The median fare for the year was $235.01.

**Fourth Quarter 2020 Air Fares**

The average U.S. domestic air fare in the fourth quarter of 2020 was $261, increasing 6.3% from an inflation-adjusted third quarter 2020 fare of $245. The number of passengers increased from 27 million originating passengers in the third quarter of 2020 quarter to 31 million passengers in the fourth quarter compared to 86 million passengers in the fourth quarter of 2019.

Adjusted for inflation (constant 2020 dollars) the average 4Q 2020 air fare was:

*   Down 27.7% from 4Q 2019 ($361)
*   Up 6.3% from 3Q 2020 ($245) 
*   Down 35.0% from 4Q 2015 ($401)

Breakout of trip types: one-way, 41% ($201); round-trip, 59% ($309).

**Fares by Airport**

[Fares by airport group](https://www.bts.gov/air-fares):

Highest: 10 airports with 43,073-49,999 originating passengers ($298).

Lowest: 16 airports with 500,000-999,999 originating passengers ($246).

**Additional data**: see [Top 100 Airports](https://www.transtats.bts.gov/AIRFARES/) or [All Airports](https://www.transtats.bts.gov/AverageFare/). First Quarter 2021 average fare data will be released July 20.

**Standard error:** Results for average fares are based on the BTS Origin & Destination Survey, a 10% sample of airline tickets used during the quarter. Averages for airports with smaller samples may be less reliable.

Note: Results for average fares are based on the BTS Origin & Destination Survey, a 10% sample of airline tickets used during the quarter. For Q4 2020 results based on all itinerary fares, the standard error is 0.30 and the median fare is $209.10.The 90% confidence interval ranges from $260.30 to $261.29. For results based on round-trip fares, the standard error is .47 and the median fare is $262.56.The 90% confidence interval ranges from $308.54 to $310.09. For results based on one-way fares, the standard error is .34 and the median fare is $158.69.The 90% confidence interval ranges from $200.00 to $201.12.

# Average Air Fares Dropped to All-Time Low in 2020

 Tuesday, April 20, 2021

**Release Number:**BTS 27-21

![Image 5](https://www.bts.gov/sites/bts.dot.gov/files/images/Air%20Fare%20Infographic%204Q2020.png)

The 2020 average domestic itinerary air fare of $292 was the lowest inflation-adjusted annual fare since the Bureau of Transportation Statistics began collecting such records in 1995, down 19% from the previous low of $359 in 2019.

In 2020, 131 million originating passengers traveled on U.S. airlines, down from 331 million in 2019.

During the year, fares dropped in the third quarter to $245, inflation-adjusted, the lowest quarterly fare on record. In the fourth quarter, fares rose to $261, up 6% from the third quarter but down 28% from the fourth quarter 2019 average fare of $361.

**Annual Air Fares**

**Inflation-adjusted**

Annual 2020 fare: $292

From Previous Year: Down 18.6% from 2019 ($359)

All Years: Down 42.6% from the highest fare for any year, $510 in 2000

Start of BTS records in 1995: Down 41.1% from 1995 ($496)

Recent high: Down 31.7% from 2014 ($428)

**Unadjusted**

Annual 2020 fare: $292

From Previous Year: Down 17.6% from 2019 ($355)

All Years: Down 25.4% from the highest fare for any year, $392 in 2014

Start of BTS records in 1995: Up .06% ($292) (compared to 69.8% consumer price index increase)

Recent low: Down 5.8% from 2009 ($310)

**Fare calculations by BTS**

**Itinerary Fares**_:_ Round-trips, but includes one-ways if no return is purchased.

**Total ticket value:** The price charged by airlines at time of ticket purchase.

**Included:**Additional taxes and fees levied by an outside entity at time of ticket purchase.

**Not included:** Fees for optional services, such as baggage fees.

**Other Revenue:** In recent years, airlines have increasingly obtained additional revenue from passenger fees, as well as from other sources. U.S. passenger airlines collected 65.1% of total operating revenue of $38.6 billion from passenger fares during the first nine months of 2020, down from 88.5% in 1990 _._

Results for average fares are based on the BTS Origin & Destination Survey, a 10% sample of airline tickets used during the quarter _._ For results based on all itinerary fares for 2020, the standard error is 0.18. The median fare for the year was $235.01.

**Fourth Quarter 2020 Air Fares**

The average U.S. domestic air fare in the fourth quarter of 2020 was $261, increasing 6.3% from an inflation-adjusted third quarter 2020 fare of $245. The number of passengers increased from 27 million originating passengers in the third quarter of 2020 quarter to 31 million passengers in the fourth quarter compared to 86 million passengers in the fourth quarter of 2019.

Adjusted for inflation (constant 2020 dollars) the average 4Q 2020 air fare was:

*   Down 27.7% from 4Q 2019 ($361)
*   Up 6.3% from 3Q 2020 ($245) 
*   Down 35.0% from 4Q 2015 ($401)

# Domestic Airfare Prices by Year, 1995-2025: Full History

Published August 1, 2026

Every figure on this page is sourced from primary U.S. government data. See our [research standards](https://truedrivingcost.com/methodology#data-sources).

Key Findings

*   In inflation-adjusted dollars, the average U.S. domestic airfare has fallen **37.3%** since 1995, from **$627.81** to **$393.33** in 2025.
*   The unadjusted (nominal) sticker price tells a different story: it actually **rose 32.5%** over the same period, from $292.19 to $387.01, which is why flying doesn't feel cheaper even though it is.
*   The steepest single-year drop was **2020, down 18.0%** in real terms as COVID-19 collapsed air travel demand.
*   The most recent data available, Q1 2026, shows fares at **$427.81**, already above the entire 2025 annual average, the sharpest early-year jump in the series.

Source: U.S. Bureau of Transportation Statistics, Annual and Quarterly U.S. Domestic Average Itinerary Fare series.

Contents

1.   Introduction
2.   The 30-Year Trend: Flying Got Cheaper, Not More Expensive
3.   The Sharpest Moves: Recessions, 9/11, and COVID
4.   The Most Recent Data: A 2026 Uptick
5.   Methodology and Caveats
6.   Data Sources

## 01 Introduction

In inflation-adjusted dollars, average U.S. domestic airfare has **fallen 37.3% since 1995** (from $627.81 to $393.33 in 2025), even though the nominal sticker price actually rose 32.5% over the same period. The Bureau of Transportation Statistics has tracked the average domestic airline fare every year since 1995, in both the dollars actually printed on the ticket and dollars adjusted for inflation. Looking at both series side by side tells a story that runs against the common assumption that flying keeps getting more expensive.

U.S. Bureau of Transportation Statistics, Annual U.S. Domestic Average Itinerary Fare, Current and Constant Dollars
## 02 The 30-Year Trend: Flying Got Cheaper, Not More Expensive

In 2025 dollars, the average domestic fare has fallen from **$627.81 in 1995 to $393.33 in 2025**, a decline of **37.3%**. But the unadjusted number most travelers actually see and remember rose over the same period, from $292.19 to $387.01, up **32.5%**. Both numbers are true at once: tickets cost more dollars today, but each of those dollars buys much more than it did in 1995, so flying has become meaningfully cheaper in real terms.

U.S. Bureau of Transportation Statistics, Annual U.S. Domestic Average Itinerary Fare series, 1995-2025. Inflation adjustment to 2026 constant dollars using the Bureau of Labor Statistics Consumer Price Index, as published by BTS.

Fig. 1 Average U.S. domestic airfare, 1995-2025. Hover to see both figures for any year. 

Inflation-adjusted (2026 $)Nominal (current $)

U.S. Bureau of Transportation Statistics

**Why this doesn't feel true.** Most people compare this year's ticket price to what they remember paying years ago, in nominal dollars, without adjusting for inflation. Since the nominal price did rise (up 32.5% since 1995), that memory isn't wrong. What it misses is that almost everything else got more expensive by more over the same period, so airfare actually became a smaller share of a typical budget.

Estimate your vehicle's driving cost using official EPA fuel economy data.

[Use the Calculator](https://truedrivingcost.com/)

## 03 The Sharpest Moves: Recessions, 9/11, and COVID

The 30-year trend isn't a smooth line. Airfares move sharply around recessions, security shocks, and the COVID-19 pandemic, usually falling faster than they later recover.

U.S. Bureau of Transportation Statistics, Annual U.S. Domestic Average Itinerary Fare series, year-over-year percent change as published by BTS

| Year | Inflation-Adjusted YoY | Nominal YoY | Context |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2001 | -8.0% | -5.4% | September 11 attacks |
| 2009 | -10.1% | -10.4% | Global financial crisis |
| 2020 | -18.0% | -17.0% | COVID-19 pandemic |
| 2022 | +14.1% | +23.2% | Post-pandemic travel rebound |

Percent changes as published by BTS, calculated from unrounded underlying values.
2020's 18.0% real-dollar drop is the single largest year-over-year decline in the entire 31-year series, a sharper collapse than either 9/11 or the 2008-2009 financial crisis. The rebound that followed was just as unusual: 2022's nominal fare jumped 23.2% in a single year, the fastest one-year increase on record, as airlines faced a rush of pent-up travel demand against reduced capacity.

## 04 The Most Recent Data: A 2026 Uptick

The most recent data available goes through the first quarter of 2026, and it shows a fare of **$427.81**, already higher than the entire 2025 annual average of $387.01 and the highest quarterly figure since before the pandemic.

U.S. Bureau of Transportation Statistics, Quarterly National Level Domestic Average Fare series, Q1 2026

**One quarter isn't a full year.** Airfares are seasonal, and a single quarter can run higher or lower than the eventual annual average. This figure is shown as the latest available data point, not as a preview of what full-year 2026 will look like.

## 05 Methodology and Caveats

All figures in this article come directly from BTS's published average fare series, without independent recalculation of the underlying survey data.

U.S. Bureau of Transportation Statistics
*   **Fares are domestic itinerary fares**: round-trip fares, or the one-way fare if no return trip was purchased, based on total ticket value including taxes and fees charged at purchase.
*   **Fares exclude optional service fees** such as checked baggage, seat selection, or change fees, and exclude frequent-flyer or "zero fares."
*   **Inflation adjustment uses the Bureau of Labor Statistics Consumer Price Index**, expressed in 2026 constant dollars, as published by BTS.
*   **Percent changes are BTS's own published figures**, calculated from unrounded underlying values, which can differ slightly from a recalculation using the rounded dollar figures shown in the table.

## 06 Data Sources

Every figure in this article comes from a U.S. government source. No proprietary, estimated, or third-party data was used.

1.   **U.S. Bureau of Transportation Statistics.** Annual U.S. Domestic Average Itinerary Fare, 1995-2026 (Current and Constant Dollars). [transtats.bts.gov](https://www.transtats.bts.gov/)
2.   **U.S. Bureau of Transportation Statistics.** Quarterly National Level Domestic Average Fare Series, 1st Quarter 2026. [transtats.bts.gov](https://www.transtats.bts.gov/)

**Disclaimer.** This article is for informational purposes only. Figures are national averages published by the Bureau of Transportation Statistics and do not reflect the price of any specific route, airline, or ticket.

### Office of Aviation Analysis

*   [Domestic Airline Consumer Airfare Report](http://www.dot.gov/policy/aviation-policy/domestic-airline-consumer-airfare-report): provides information about average prices being paid by consumers in the top 1,000 domestic city pair markets in the continental United States

### Questions? Contact Randall Keizer

Office of Aviation Analysis  
 1200 New Jersey Ave, SE  
 Washington,DC 20590  
 United States

* * *

### Bureau of Transportation Statistics (BTS)

*   [Airline Origin and Destination Survey (DB1B)](https://www.transtats.bts.gov/)- click on "Aviation" then "Airline Origin & Destination Survey" -a 10% sample of airline tickets from reporting carriers including origin, destination and other itinerary details of passengers transported. As of July 2025, carriers will begin reporting 40% of their tickets, rather than 10%. [Click here for more information.](https://www.bts.gov/OD-40)

*   Origin and Destination Survey: DB1BMarket (click "Download"):average fares by airport pairs (or city pairs)

1.   Select the following fields:

    *   Origin

    *   OriginCityMarketID

    *   Dest

    *   ​DestCityMarketID

    *   Passengers

    *   MktFare

2.   Filter:

    *   Geography (by either origin or destination state),

    *   Year

    *   Quarter (N ote: you can only download one quarter at a time)

3.   Filter out fares below a certain value (e.g. $50) to eliminate flights that just contain taxes and fees but no actual base fare. This is how BTS calculates the average fares.

4.   Download data and multiply Passengers x Market Fare for each row to get Total Fare

5.   Sum the Passengers column and sum your newly created Total Fare column

6.   Divide the Total Fare by the total number of Passengers

Fares include only the price paid at the time of the ticket purchase and do not include other fees, such as baggage fees, paid at the airport or onboard the aircraft. The average cost of a domestic plane ticket is $428 as of the first quarter of 2026, the most recent period for which there is data from the Department of Transportation. That's up from $404 in the previous quarter and about $31 higher than the average price recorded in the first quarter of 2025.

The average cost of an international economy-class plane ticket is $1,217, according to FCM and Corporate Traveler. Keep in mind the cost of international airfare fluctuates more than domestic plane tickets depending on destination. It costs much more to fly to Japan from the United States than it does to fly to Canada, for example.

How much a plane ticket costs depends on a number of factors, including the price of jet fuel, passenger demand, seat capacity, the number of carriers flying a route, and economic conditions like inflation and consumer confidence.

Motley Fool Money has the latest data on the average plane ticket costs, broken down by airport and route.

## The average cost of a domestic plane ticket

The average cost of a domestic flight in the U.S. as of the first quarter of 2026 is $428. That's $31 more than prices recorded a year ago.

Domestic airfare plummeted to around $250 on average in the second and third quarters of 2020, during the height of the COVID-19 pandemic. The cost of domestic flights have since rebounded and have stayed above $350 on average since the second quarter of 2022.

The chart below shows the average cost of domestic airfare over time.

### Jet fuel prices are 30% higher than a year ago

Jet fuel is one of the largest operating costs for airlines, and its price directly influences what passengers pay for tickets.

Jet fuel prices in North America rose 30% in the week ending on July 3, 2026 from the year before, while the global average climbed 32% to $119 per barrel, according to the IATA Jet Fuel Price Monitor. That spike followed the start of the Iran conflict, although prices have since come down from their April and May peaks.

### The average cost of domestic airfare in the U.S. by airport

The table below shows the average cost of domestic airfare by origin airport in the first quarter of 2026.

The most expensive flights originate from smaller and more remote airports, such as those in Guam and Alaska. The cheapest flights originate from secondary or regional airports served by low-cost carriers with limited routes. The busiest airports -- LAX, ORD, DEN -- have average domestic airfare costs close to the national average.

The most expensive domestic U.S. flights originate from Guam and Alaska. Domestic flights out of Guam International airport are the priciest, costing $1,576 on average. Unalaska Airport in the Alaskan Aleutian Islands is the most expensive departure point in the 50 states, with average domestic airfare of $1,114.

The most expensive airport to depart from for domestic travel in the continental U.S. is Centennial Airport in Colorado. The average cost of domestic airfare out of APA is $992.

The least expensive airports to fly out of for domestic travel are spread out across secondary and regional airports across the U.S. They include Chuathbaluk Airport in Alaska ($60 on average), Block Island State Airport in Rhode Island ($66), and Healy River Airport in Alaska ($70), according to the Bureau of Transportation Statistics data from the first quarter of 2026.

### The most and least expensive domestic flights in the U.S.

The most expensive city-pair flights within the U.S. cover long distances and sometimes originate or land at smaller airports. New York-San Francisco was the most expensive route in the fourth quarter of 2025, averaging $516. Los Angeles to New York was the second most expensive ($464), followed by Atlanta to Salt Lake City ($439).

The least expensive domestic routes are served by ultra-low-cost carriers, like Allegiant and Spirit, connect secondary airports and leisure routes, and tend to be between mid-size cities. The cheapest domestic flight in the fourth quarter of 2025 was Knoxville, Tennessee to Sanford, Florida, averaging $99 a ticket.

## International airfare price statistics

The average cost of an international plane ticket departing from the United States is $1,217 according to FCM and Corporate Traveler. International plane ticket prices vary widely based on route. A flight from Texas to Mexico or New York to Canada will be much cheaper than flying from Florida to France or California to Australia.

## How to save on plane tickets

Planning ahead and using credit cards and apps can make flights more affordable. Here are a few tips to help you save.

*   **Use a travel credit card or credit card points:** Many travel credit cards offer points or miles for everyday purchases which can be redeemed for flights. Some cards include perks like a free checked bag or airport lounge access. Motley Fool Money has breakdowns of [the best travel credit cards](https://www.fool.com/money/credit-cards/best-travel-rewards-credit-cards/?luri=%2Fresearch%2Faverage-cost-of-airfare%2F&furi=%2Fresearch%2Faverage-cost-of-airfare%2F&fuuid=8049a7ad-66d1-4ebd-9b8c-abdeeeddbf32&luuid=8049a7ad-66d1-4ebd-9b8c-abdeeeddbf32&ltyp=txt) and [the best airline credit cards](https://www.fool.com/money/credit-cards/best-airline-credit-cards/?luri=%2Fresearch%2Faverage-cost-of-airfare%2F&furi=%2Fresearch%2Faverage-cost-of-airfare%2F&fuuid=8049a7ad-66d1-4ebd-9b8c-abdeeeddbf32&luuid=8049a7ad-66d1-4ebd-9b8c-abdeeeddbf32&ltyp=txt) if you want to dive deeper.
*   **Monitor plane ticket prices:** Flight prices can change daily, so setting up price alerts can alert you to a deal when prices drop. Be patient and let the deals come to you.
*   **Avoid peak travel days:** Airline tickets are usually more expensive on the weekends and during holidays. If you can be flexible, look to book mid-week, particularly Tuesday or Wednesday, to snag a cheaper seat.

A little planning and flexibility can go a long way in finding a cheaper flight -- which keeps more money in your pocket for the fun parts of your trip.

The average cost of a domestic plane ticket is $428 as of the first quarter of 2026, the most recent period for which there is data from the Department of Transportation. That's up from $404 in the previous quarter and about $31 higher than the average price recorded in the first quarter of 2025.

The average cost of an international economy-class plane ticket is $1,217, according to FCM and Corporate Traveler. Keep in mind the cost of international airfare fluctuates more than domestic plane tickets depending on destination. It costs much more to fly to Japan from the United States than it does to fly to Canada, for example.

How much a plane ticket costs depends on a number of factors, including the price of jet fuel, passenger demand, seat capacity, the number of carriers flying a route, and economic conditions like inflation and consumer confidence.

Motley Fool Money has the latest data on the average plane ticket costs, broken down by airport and route.

## The average cost of a domestic plane ticket

The average cost of a domestic flight in the U.S. as of the first quarter of 2026 is $428. That's $31 more than prices recorded a year ago.

Domestic airfare plummeted to around $250 on average in the second and third quarters of 2020, during the height of the COVID-19 pandemic. The cost of domestic flights have since rebounded and have stayed above $350 on average since the second quarter of 2022.

The chart below shows the average cost of domestic airfare over time.

### Jet fuel prices are 30% higher than a year ago

Jet fuel is one of the largest operating costs for airlines, and its price directly influences what passengers pay for tickets.

Jet fuel prices in North America rose 30% in the week ending on July 3, 2026 from the year before, while the global average climbed 32% to $119 per barrel, according to the IATA Jet Fuel Price Monitor. That spike followed the start of the Iran conflict, although prices have since come down from their April and May peaks.

### The average cost of domestic airfare in the U.S. by airport

The table below shows the average cost of domestic airfare by origin airport in the first quarter of 2026.

The most expensive flights originate from smaller and more remote airports, such as those in Guam and Alaska. The cheapest flights originate from secondary or regional airports served by low-cost carriers with limited routes. The busiest airports -- LAX, ORD, DEN -- have average domestic airfare costs close to the national average.

The most expensive domestic U.S. flights originate from Guam and Alaska. Domestic flights out of Guam International airport are the priciest, costing $1,576 on average. Unalaska Airport in the Alaskan Aleutian Islands is the most expensive departure point in the 50 states, with average domestic airfare of $1,114.

The most expensive airport to depart from for domestic travel in the continental U.S. is Centennial Airport in Colorado. The average cost of domestic airfare out of APA is $992.

The least expensive airports to fly out of for domestic travel are spread out across secondary and regional airports across the U.S. They include Chuathbaluk Airport in Alaska ($60 on average), Block Island State Airport in Rhode Island ($66), and Healy River Airport in Alaska ($70), according to the Bureau of Transportation Statistics data from the first quarter of 2026.

### The most and least expensive domestic flights in the U.S.

The most expensive city-pair flights within the U.S. cover long distances and sometimes originate or land at smaller airports. New York-San Francisco was the most expensive route in the fourth quarter of 2025, averaging $516. Los Angeles to New York was the second most expensive ($464), followed by Atlanta to Salt Lake City ($439).

The least expensive domestic routes are served by ultra-low-cost carriers, like Allegiant and Spirit, connect secondary airports and leisure routes, and tend to be between mid-size cities. The cheapest domestic flight in the fourth quarter of 2025 was Knoxville, Tennessee to Sanford, Florida, averaging $99 a ticket.

## International airfare price statistics

The average cost of an international plane ticket departing from the United States is $1,217 according to FCM and Corporate Traveler. International plane ticket prices vary widely based on route. A flight from Texas to Mexico or New York to Canada will be much cheaper than flying from Florida to France or California to Australia.

## How to save on plane tickets

Planning ahead and using credit cards and apps can make flights more affordable. Here are a few tips to help you save.

*   **Use a travel credit card or credit card points:** Many travel credit cards offer points or miles for everyday purchases which can be redeemed for flights. Some cards include perks like a free checked bag or airport lounge access. Motley Fool Money has breakdowns of [the best travel credit cards](https://www.fool.com/money/credit-cards/best-travel-rewards-credit-cards/?luri=%2Fresearch%2Faverage-cost-of-airfare%2F&furi=%2Fresearch%2Faverage-cost-of-airfare%2F&fuuid=8049a7ad-66d1-4ebd-9b8c-abdeeeddbf32&luuid=8049a7ad-66d1-4ebd-9b8c-abdeeeddbf32&ltyp=txt) and [the best airline credit cards](https://www.fool.com/money/credit-cards/best-airline-credit-cards/?luri=%2Fresearch%2Faverage-cost-of-airfare%2F&furi=%2Fresearch%2Faverage-cost-of-airfare%2F&fuuid=8049a7ad-66d1-4ebd-9b8c-abdeeeddbf32&luuid=8049a7ad-66d1-4ebd-9b8c-abdeeeddbf32&ltyp=txt) if you want to dive deeper.
*   **Monitor plane ticket prices:** Flight prices can change daily, so setting up price alerts can alert you to a deal when prices drop. Be patient and let the deals come to you.
*   **Avoid peak travel days:** Airline tickets are usually more expensive on the weekends and during holidays. If you can be flexible, look to book mid-week, particularly Tuesday or Wednesday, to snag a cheaper seat.

A little planning and flexibility can go a long way in finding a cheaper flight -- which keeps more money in your pocket for the fun parts of your trip.

# Warm Places to Visit in November: 3 Cool Off by December

Fourteen US and Caribbean destinations that clear a 71°F warmth floor, measured on NOAA's own November air and sea readings, with three that turn noticeably cooler the moment December starts.

Last verified: August 2026•Guide•By [Endless Travel Plans Research Team](https://www.endlesstravelplans.com/about/methodology)

![Image 1: Warm Places to Visit in November: 3 Cool Off by December](https://endlesstravelplans.nyc3.cdn.digitaloceanspaces.com/articles/content/obx-vs-myrtle-beach-comparison-hero.jpg)

## Quick Answer

*   🌴 The top-scoring warm place to visit in November for a family of four is San Juan, Puerto Rico: an 86.1°F average high and 84.6°F mean sea temperature, both measured across the whole month (as of August 2026, source: NOAA).
*   🌡️ Every destination in our ranking averages a daily high of at least 71°F in November; anything colder didn't clear the bar, National Weather Service and NOAA climate normals (as of August 2026, source: NOAA).
*   🏄 Three of the desert picks below turn noticeably cooler once December starts, and the drop is big enough to change which week you'd actually want to book.
*   🏖️ Not every "warm" pick on this list has anywhere to swim at all, and three that do read under the swim-warm line by enough to keep kids out of it.
*   🧭 Skip this guide if you're planning a December trip instead (our [warm places to visit in December guide](https://www.endlesstravelplans.com/guides/family-travel/warm-winter-family-vacations-december) covers that month) or you've already picked the Caribbean and just need an age-based pick (our [Caribbean islands by age guide](https://www.endlesstravelplans.com/destinations/caribbean/best-caribbean-islands-december-by-age) ranks that).
*   🧮 Run your own dates through the [family budget calculator](https://www.endlesstravelplans.com/tools/budget-calculator) before booking; NOAA measures temperature, not what four plane tickets and a week of hotel rooms cost.
*   👉 Below: which three ranked picks fail their own water test under Where Is Best for a Beach Holiday in November, and which three warm-weather picks cool off fastest once December arrives under What Changes in December.

Somebody's toddler is already asking to swim off a Myrtle Beach hotel balcony in November, going by how mild the afternoon feels on the boardwalk. As of August 2026, NOAA's own Springmaid Pier station put that water at 62.0°F for the whole month, the kind of number a wetsuit crowd tolerates and small kids don't. The ranking below sorts every warm-sounding November pick by what NOAA actually measured, not by what the air feels like on the sand; start with how the score is built, then run your dates through the family budget calculator.

## Where Is the Warmest Place to Go in November?

San Juan, Puerto Rico tops our ranking on both numbers that matter for a family trip: an 86.1°F average daily high and a 74.9°F average low across November, and, for the beach afternoon, a mean sea temperature of 84.6°F measured hourly through the whole month (as of August 2026, source: NOAA). Charlotte Amalie sits close behind at 86.8°F air and 84.5°F water, close enough that either answers "warmest" honestly.

Myrtle Beach turns up constantly on "warm in November" lists, and its own numbers say otherwise: a 66.4°F November air average and NOAA-measured water at 62.0°F, both under the 71°F floor this guide applies to every pick (as of August 2026, source: NOAA). Warm-sounding and warm are not the same claim.

## How the November Swim Score Works: Air, Water, Crowds, Cost, Kid-Fit

We built a floor before we built a ranking. A destination's November average daily high has to reach 71°F for it to appear on our table at all; that line sits in a real gap in the NOAA data, between San Antonio's 71.7°F and San Diego's 70.7°F, rather than on a round number picked for convenience. Applying it consistently costs four destinations their spot: San Diego, Charleston SC, Las Vegas and Myrtle Beach itself, all covered further down under Where Is Best for a Beach Holiday in November.

A family of four here means two adults and two kids, ages six and ten, every time we quote a fare block. Everything that clears the floor is then scored on five factors, each worth 0 to 5 points, for a maximum of 25: Air, Water, Crowds, Cost and Kid-Fit. All five come off published data, with the anchors printed below, and it's the same five-factor idea our [family vacation cost index](https://www.endlesstravelplans.com/guides/family-travel/family-vacation-cost-index-2026) uses on the pricing side.

### What each factor is worth

| Factor | What it measures | 5 points | 3 points | 1 point | Where the number comes from |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Air | The 1991-2020 November normal high | 85.0°F or hotter | 77.0 to 79.9°F | 71.0 to 73.9°F | NOAA NCEI |
| Water | Mean sea temperature across November 2025 | 82.0°F or warmer | 75.0 to 77.9°F | A coastal station under 72.0°F | NOAA CO-OPS |
| Crowds | The nearest airport's 2025 US domestic passenger rank | Outside the top 60 | Ranks 25 to 39 | Ranks 6 to 14 | US Bureau of Transportation Statistics |
| Cost | Average round-trip domestic fare from that city, Q1 2026 | Under $325 | $375 to $424 | $465 or more | US Bureau of Transportation Statistics |

Crowds and Cost both come off one Bureau of Transportation Statistics release, which ranks US airports by 2025 domestic passengers and prints an average fare beside each (as of August 2026, source: US Bureau of Transportation Statistics). That fare is an origin-city average across every route, not a quote for your dates.

![Image 2: A family checking a beach forecast on a phone before a November trip, the step this method replaces with NOAA data.](https://endlesstravelplans.nyc3.cdn.digitaloceanspaces.com/articles/content/beach-destinations-children-2.jpg)

Rain enters once, inside Kid-Fit. NOAA's November precipitation normal decides whether a warm afternoon happens outside or in a hotel lobby, and it splits the desert picks from the Caribbean ones harder than air does. What we left out is anything we'd have to guess at: hotel rates, park queues, hurricane odds. A factor you can't look up isn't a factor, it's a preference.

## The Ranking: 14 Warm November Destinations, Air and Water Measured

Fourteen destinations clear the 71°F floor, and the score sorts them differently than air alone does. Three win on three different kinds of trip, so here they are first.

### 1 San Juan, Puerto Rico

21 out of 25. Best overall, and the cheapest seat in the top five
Top marks on Air at 86.1°F and Water at 84.6°F, both NOAA-measured across the whole month (as of August 2026, source: NOAA), and the cheapest average fare in the top five, $320.09 a seat (as of August 2026, source: US Bureau of Transportation Statistics). What holds it to 21 is Kid-Fit: 7.37 inches of November rain, the wettest month on our table.

### 2 South Padre Island, Texas

20 out of 25. Best mainland pick, no passport, quietest arrival in the top five
It comes within a point of San Juan from the opposite direction. 80.3°F air, 78.2°F water at NOAA's Port Isabel station, and 1.76 inches of November rain against San Juan's 7.37 (as of August 2026, source: NOAA). Harlingen, the nearest airport, ranked 132nd in the country for domestic passengers last year and averages $340.60 a seat (as of August 2026, source: US Bureau of Transportation Statistics).

### 3 Charlotte Amalie, US Virgin Islands

19 out of 25. Warmest air on the page, at the price that comes with it

The six points it drops go to a $433.30 seat (as of August 2026, source: US Bureau of Transportation Statistics) and 5.30 inches of November rain (source: NOAA).

## Where Is Best for a Beach Holiday in November? (Three of the Ranked Picks Fail the Water Test)

Air temperature alone lies to you about swimming. Fort Myers averages 81.3°F in the air, but NOAA's own Fort Myers station reads a 73.2°F mean sea temperature for November, under the 75°F line we use for "swim-warm" (as of August 2026, source: NOAA). Tampa tells the same story from its Clearwater Beach water station: 78.9°F air against 69.7°F water, and Corpus Christi makes three, 76.1°F air against 73.4°F in the bay at NOAA's USS Lexington station (as of August 2026, source: NOAA). All three are warm places. None is a warm ocean in November, not by NOAA's own water reading.

### Five of the Ranked Picks Have No Water Reading at All

Here's the finding worth more than the water-test count: five of the fourteen warmest places on our own table, Palm Springs, Orlando, Phoenix, Tucson and San Antonio, have no CO-OPS water reading at all because they are desert or inland. They don't fail a swim test. They were never in one. A parent who searches "warm places to visit in november" and pictures a beach is picturing the wrong trip for over a third of this list, and nobody tells them that up front.

![Image 3: Kids playing in shallow warm-weather surf, the swim-warm scenario that only about half of this list's picks actually offer.](https://endlesstravelplans.nyc3.cdn.digitaloceanspaces.com/articles/content/beach-destinations-children-4.jpg)

These four commonly suggested picks never reach the ranked table because their November air average sits under our 71°F floor, not because of anything to do with water:

As of August 2026, source: NOAA.

We'll be blunt: if a beach afternoon in the water is the goal, eight of our fourteen ranked picks can't deliver it and four more familiar names don't clear the warmth bar at all. San Juan, Charlotte Amalie, Honolulu, Miami, Key West and South Padre Island are the only picks here where both numbers back up the word "warm."

## Where Is Warm and Cheap in November in the USA?

Phoenix is the pick most lists call cheap, and no Phoenix lodging or destination source published a 2026 week-for-four total as of August 2026, so this guide prices the part a national statistics agency does publish. On fares, Orlando and San Juan average the two cheapest seats on this page, $304.41 and $320.09, while Corpus Christi, which sounds like the budget Gulf answer, averages $509.26 and Phoenix sits at $398.66 (as of August 2026, source: US Bureau of Transportation Statistics). Cheap to fly to and cheap to spend a week in are not the same list; our [warm December guide](https://www.endlesstravelplans.com/guides/family-travel/warm-winter-family-vacations-december) carries lodging-inclusive December ranges for Phoenix and Puerto Rico.

Our [affordable winter family vacations guide](https://www.endlesstravelplans.com/guides/family-travel/affordable-winter-family-vacations) prices the same trade-off for December.

The lodging half of that basket is the part no national dataset publishes, which is why Table 2 stops at the fare; price it on your own dates before you commit to a destination on fares alone.

## What Caribbean Island Is Hot in November?

San Juan and Charlotte Amalie are effectively tied at the top: 86.1°F and 86.8°F air, 84.6°F and 84.5°F water respectively, both measured by NOAA through November (as of August 2026, source: NOAA). Either answers "hot" honestly. Neither island's tourism board published a 2026 week-for-four figure as of August 2026, so the fare is what separates them on cost: $320.09 against $433.30 a seat (as of August 2026, source: US Bureau of Transportation Statistics).

Is one actually better than the other? Not on temperature. The gap between them is far too small to pick a trip on, so pick on flight availability and lodging style rather than a number this close.

You can [see current San Juan snorkel and day-tour options on Viator](https://www.viator.com/searchResults/all?text=San%20Juan%20Puerto%20Rico%20snorkel%20tour&pid=P00254785&mcid=42383&medium=link&subId=web_warmnov_caribbean_viator) to compare against whatever your hotel desk quotes once you're there.

Our [Caribbean islands by age guide](https://www.endlesstravelplans.com/destinations/caribbean/best-caribbean-islands-december-by-age) ranks these same islands by kids' age band if you're choosing for December instead of November, since the swim window and the surge pricing both shift once the calendar turns.

## Where to Go in November on a Budget, and Where Is Hot in November but Cheap?

Tucson against Phoenix is the real desert budget question, and the score splits them: Tucson takes 12 out of 25, Phoenix 9. Most of that gap is elbow room. Tucson's airport ranked 74th in the country for domestic passengers last year against Phoenix's 11th, and Phoenix is one of only two picks on this page inside the national top fifteen (as of August 2026, source: US Bureau of Transportation Statistics). Phoenix wins part of it back on the seat, $398.66 against Tucson's $454.74 (as of August 2026, source: US Bureau of Transportation Statistics). Neither city published a 2026 week-for-four total, so treat Tucson as the quieter option, not a proven cheaper one.

Whichever desert city you pick, the week you book moves more money than the state does, and that is the next section.

## Thanksgiving Week vs Early November: The Line That Splits the Month

Thanksgiving 2026 falls on Thursday, November 26, near the late end of the fourth-Thursday window that runs from November 22 to November 28, which pushes the early-November shoulder to more than three full weeks before the surge starts.

Thanksgiving-week fares run well above early-November pricing on the same routes, and this guide prices the non-Thanksgiving weeks only. If your dates are flexible at all, that's still the single biggest lever on this page, bigger than the difference between any two destinations on Table 1. Our [Thanksgiving family vacation ideas guide](https://www.endlesstravelplans.com/guides/family-travel/thanksgiving-family-vacation-ideas) ranks Thanksgiving-specific trips directly if that's the week you're locked into; this guide prices the rest of November instead.

## What Changes in December (and Which Picks Move)

Three of the fourteen ranked picks cool off fast enough that the calendar actually changes the trip: Phoenix drops 10.3°F to a 66.2°F December average, Tucson drops 9.6°F to 65.5°F, and Palm Springs drops 9.5°F to 69.2°F (as of August 2026, source: NOAA). Every other pick on our table loses less than 9 degrees; San Antonio, the next steepest, drops 7.0°F.

Why the desert picks? Dry desert air loses heat fast once the sun angle drops, while the ocean holds island warmth; San Juan and Charlotte Amalie move under 2°F each.

If a desert pick is on your shortlist, book it for November. The same trip in December runs colder, and the calendar is the only thing that changed.

## Picking Your November Week

Everything on Table 1 works in November, but not the same way; the right pick depends on what you want out of the trip.

## Where Is the Warmest Place to Go in November?

San Juan, Puerto Rico tops our ranking on both numbers that matter for a family trip: an 86.1°F average daily high and a 74.9°F average low across November, and, for the beach afternoon, a mean sea temperature of 84.6°F measured hourly through the whole month (as of August 2026, source: NOAA). Charlotte Amalie sits close behind at 86.8°F air and 84.5°F water, close enough that either answers "warmest" honestly.

Myrtle Beach turns up constantly on "warm in November" lists, and its own numbers say otherwise: a 66.4°F November air average and NOAA-measured water at 62.0°F, both under the 71°F floor this guide applies to every pick (as of August 2026, source: NOAA). Warm-sounding and warm are not the same claim.

## How the November Swim Score Works: Air, Water, Crowds, Cost, Kid-Fit

We built a floor before we built a ranking. A destination's November average daily high has to reach 71°F for it to appear on our table at all; that line sits in a real gap in the NOAA data, between San Antonio's 71.7°F and San Diego's 70.7°F, rather than on a round number picked for convenience. Applying it consistently costs four destinations their spot: San Diego, Charleston SC, Las Vegas and Myrtle Beach itself, all covered further down under Where Is Best for a Beach Holiday in November.

A family of four here means two adults and two kids, ages six and ten, every time we quote a fare block. Everything that clears the floor is then scored on five factors, each worth 0 to 5 points, for a maximum of 25: Air, Water, Crowds, Cost and Kid-Fit. All five come off published data, with the anchors printed below, and it's the same five-factor idea our [family vacation cost index](https://www.endlesstravelplans.com/guides/family-travel/family-vacation-cost-index-2026) uses on the pricing side.

All three are warm places. None is a warm ocean in November, not by NOAA's own water reading.

Here's the finding worth more than the water-test count: five of the fourteen warmest places on our own table, Palm Springs, Orlando, Phoenix, Tucson and San Antonio, have no CO-OPS water reading at all because they are desert or inland. San Juan and Charlotte Amalie are effectively tied at the top: 86.1°F and 86.8°F air, 84.6°F and 84.5°F water respectively, both measured by NOAA through November (as of August 2026, source: NOAA). Tucson against Phoenix is the real desert budget question, and the score splits them: Tucson takes 12 out of 25, Phoenix 9. Most of that gap is elbow room. Thanksgiving 2026 falls on Thursday, November 26, near the late end of the fourth-Thursday window that runs from November 22 to November 28, which pushes the early-November shoulder to more than three full weeks before the surge starts.

Thanksgiving-week fares run well above early-November pricing on the same routes, and this guide prices the non-Thanksgiving weeks only. Where is the warmest place to go in November?

San Juan, Puerto Rico and Charlotte Amalie, USVI are effectively tied at the top of our ranking, both averaging 86°F-plus air highs and mean sea temperatures above 84°F across November (as of August 2026, source: NOAA). After enduring long and uncertain pandemic quarantines and shutdowns, Americans have the traveling bug again — in big numbers. A recent [Forbes Advisor Survey](https://www.forbes.com/advisor/credit-cards/inflation-has-not-deflated-americas-travel-plans-2023/) found that 49% of people polled planned on traveling more in 2023 than in 2022. Meanwhile, the popular travel planning site [The Vacationer](https://thevacationer.com/summer-travel-survey-2023/) reported that 85% of Americans surveyed planned at least one trip before Labor Day. It’s a safe bet that travel won’t suddenly fall off the map when cool weather comes.

With vast numbers of people getting on flights and going places, that means extra crowds and cost pressure on many well-known big-city destinations that routinely attract millions.

We evaluated five data points to locate cities that offer lovely travel experiences without breaking the bank. If you’re in the market for a unique adventure but want to save money for everyday expenses, this list of 13 Underrated Travel Destinations to Get the Most Bang for Your Buck is a great way to start. Enjoy the journey!

 Navigate This Article:

## Cities Map

If you’re optimistic, you’re likely to agree that nearly every American city and town has something to offer the budget-minded traveler, especially if experience rather than extravagance is the goal.

After all, no matter how much money is at stake, travel can always be about immersing yourself in a new environment and connecting with new people. It can be the ultimate learning experience!

![Image 9: Map of cities](https://www.cardrates.com/images/uploads/2023/08/US-city-locator-map.jpg?width=723&height=384)

Map of cities included in our rankings.

There are plenty of experiences here. To rank our list, we looked at the cost of lodging, roundtrip flights, and food prices in cities known for their low cost of living, walkability, and popularity of restaurants and parks. Dig in and explore!

## 1. Cleveland, Ohio

Like many American cities, Cleveland has reinvented itself a few times over the years, and now it’s a place where the melting pot produces a heady mix. History intersects with innovation, old-timers learn newcomers’ ways, and the city never stops looking to the future.

![Image 10: Cleveland, OH](https://www.cardrates.com/images/uploads/2023/08/Cleveland-Night-Skyline.jpg?width=723&height=384)

“[Cleveland Night Skyline](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Cleveland,_Ohio_Night_Skyline_(9703394770).jpg)” by Eric Drost, licensed under [CC BY 2.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0/)

Strolling the Westside Market is a blast, even if you plan to go out for dinner. Do so, and you’ll learn about Cleveland’s diversity through its food. Parks, natural spaces, historic sites, museums, galleries, and ethnic neighborhoods abound.

Visit the Cleveland Public Library for its gorgeous architecture and stay for tours and experiences to help the whole family engage with a city that’s never the same twice.

![Image 11: Cleveland, OH facts](https://www.cardrates.com/images/uploads/2023/08/Cleveland-stats.jpg?width=723&height=160)

## 2. Baltimore, Maryland

Do you know why Baltimore calls its NFL football team the Ravens? Because one of the city’s favorite sons wrote a poem. You may have heard of “The Raven” and its spooky author, Edgar Allan Poe, considered the city’s most famous man of letters and one of America’s best.

![Image 12: Baltimore, MD](https://www.cardrates.com/images/uploads/2023/08/Baltimore-Center.jpg?width=723&height=381)

“[Baltimore Center](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Baltimore_center.jpg)” by Patrick Gillespie, licensed under [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

Walk the cobblestones of Baltimore’s historic Fell’s Point neighborhood to connect with the past as Poe might have experienced it. Or check out the maritime delights of the Inner Harbor, with the National Aquarium nearby.

The Baltimore Museum of Art and the Peabody Library provide cultural elevation, and the Basilica of the National Shrine of the Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary is a prime example of vintage religious architecture.

One more thing: Visiting Poe’s Gravesite and Memorial is a must.

![Image 13: Baltimore, MD facts](https://www.cardrates.com/images/uploads/2023/08/Baltimore-stats.jpg?width=723&height=160)

## 3. Grand Rapids, Michigan

Grand Rapids is one of those cities that deserves more attention than it gets, especially from folks interested in its rich history as a furniture-making center. That made it a center for labor conflict and unionization as well. And Grand Rapids has more connection with Michigan’s automobile industry than you might think.

![Image 14: Grand Rapids, MI](https://www.cardrates.com/images/uploads/2023/08/Grand-Rapids-in-April-2022.jpg?width=723&height=385)

“[Grand Rapids in April 2022](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Grand_Rapids_April_2022.jpg)” by WMrapids, licensed under [CC BY 1.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/1.0/)

The city’s Heritage Hill Historic District hearkens back to the luxury that once was in Grand Rapids. The Calvin Ecosystem Preserve and Native Gardens points even further into the past, when the area was home to indigenous peoples. And the majestic Cathedral of Saint Andrew will surely make your visit to this underrated midwestern city more contemplative.

![Image 15: Grand Rapids, MI facts](https://www.cardrates.com/images/uploads/2023/08/Grand-Rapids-stats.jpg?width=723&height=160)

## 4. Metairie, Louisiana

Metairie is just part of the New Orleans metro area in some ways, but in others, it’s a destination all to itself. It sits on an ancient natural levee on the Mississippi River that Acolapissa Native Americans used as a road. Now it’s a place where Cajun and Creole cultures influence — and are influenced by — some of Louisiana’s many migrant newcomers.

![Image 16: Metairie, LA](https://www.cardrates.com/images/uploads/2023/08/Sunset-from-the-Danziger-Bridge-Looking-Toward-Metairie.jpg?width=723&height=385)

“[Sunset from the Danziger Bridge Looking Toward Metairie](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Sunset_from_the_Danziger_Bridge_looking_towards_Metairie_3.jpg)” by thepipe26, licensed under [CC BY 2.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0/)

Hang out in Lafreniere Park to get away from it all and perhaps swelter in the subtropical heat of Lake Pontchartrain and the Mississippi Delta. Or visit the Bucktown district on the shores of the lake and catch the sunset at the nearby Bucktown Marsh Boardwalk. There’s a ton to do if you want to escape NOLa’s crowds.

![Image 17: Metairie, LA facts](https://www.cardrates.com/images/uploads/2023/08/Metairie-stats-1.jpg?width=723&height=160)

## 5. Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

When you visit Philadelphia, you’ll come away with a sense of it as a working city. Sure, Philly will always have status as a center for the American Revolution and the Constitution, and a visit to the Liberty Bell is a must.

![Image 18: Philadelphia, PA](https://www.cardrates.com/images/uploads/2023/08/Philadelphia-from-South-Street-Bridge.jpg?width=723&height=384)

“[Philadelphia from South Street Bridge](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Philadelphia_from_South_Street_Bridge_July_2016_panorama_3.jpg)” by King of Hearts, licensed under [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)

But as you’re enjoying the sites, you may suddenly realize that hustle and bustle is the name of the game in Philadelphia. After centuries of leadership and transformation, Philadelphians persist in continually reinventing themselves.

When you’re done with Independence Hall and the other historic sites, check out the Cathedral Basilica of Saints Peter and Paul for a different view of history or get soundblasted by the unique Wanamaker Organ. Philly has much to offer.

![Image 19: Philadelphia, PA facts](https://www.cardrates.com/images/uploads/2023/08/Philadelphia-stats.jpg?width=723&height=160)

## 6. St. Petersburg/Clearwater, FL

No, this isn’t a ringer. We’re down in Florida now to bring you an environment challenging to summarize in a hundred words. Clearwater may be one of Florida’s quintessential beach towns, but when you’re ready for a stretch and some shade, take a walk at Ream Wilson Clearwater Trail. Your legs (and possibly your dog) will thank you.

![Image 20: Vinoy Basin in St. Petersburg, FL](https://www.cardrates.com/images/uploads/2023/08/Vinoy-Basin-St-Petersburg.jpg?width=723&height=384)

“[Vinoy Basin – St. Petersburg](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Vinoy_Basin_-_St._Petersburg,_Florida_-_panoramio.jpg)” by steve shawn, licensed under [CC BY 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/)

Meanwhile, further south on the Pinellas peninsula between Tampa Bay and the Gulf of Mexico, St. Petersburg stands as a monument to American exuberance. Museums, galleries, preserves, and parks abound. Or visit the St. Petersburg Saturday Morning Market for a thick slice of St. Pete you’ll want to take home with you.

![Image 21: St. Petersburg, FL facts](https://www.cardrates.com/images/uploads/2023/08/Saint-Petersburg-stats.jpg?width=723&height=160)

## 7. St. Louis, Missouri

The Home of the Gateway Arch presents visitors with wide-open vistas looking west and the historic vigor of a river town looking east. Civil War general and US president Ulysses S. Grant called St. Louis home (visit the Ulysses S. Grant National Historical Site to learn about this seminal American figure). And Grant’s Farm on the outskirts of town offers vivid Victorian architecture and a family-focused outdoor learning experience.

![Image 22: St. Louis, MO](https://www.cardrates.com/images/uploads/2023/08/St-Louis-on-the-Mississippi-River-by-Night.jpg?width=723&height=384)

“[St. Louis on the Mississippi River by Night](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:St_Louis_night_expblend.jpg)” by Daniel Schwen, licensed under [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)

St. Louis is also a cultural center. Visit the Cathedral Basilica of St. Louis for a stunning and unprecedentedly extensive mosaic installation. The Saint Louis Art Museum and the Saint Louis Science Center are top-notch. And Laumeier Sculpture Park may challenge your concept of art.

![Image 23: St. Louis, MO facts](https://www.cardrates.com/images/uploads/2023/08/Saint-Louis-stats.jpg?width=723&height=160)

## 8. Cincinnati, Ohio

Cincinnati is one of those river towns steeped in history yet impressive for its modernity. It’s well worth a visit for its Roebling Suspension Bridge, which straddles the Ohio River and the border between Ohio and Kentucky, which were very different states before the Civil War.

![Image 24: Cincinnati, OH](https://www.cardrates.com/images/uploads/2023/08/Downtown-Cincinnati-from-Mount-Adams.jpg?width=723&height=385)

“[Downtown Cincinnati from Mount Adams](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Downtown_Cincinnati_viewed_from_Mt._Adams_(cropped).jpg)” by EEJCC, licensed under [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

The Spring Grove Cemetery and Arboretum is a gorgeous natural and wildlife area that also offers a sampling of the past. Smale Riverfront Park has beautiful formal gardens and places to run and be free.

Findlay Market is great for browsing even if you’re not going to purchase. The Cathedral Basilica of the Assumption offers solace. And Cincinnati is home to the William Howard Taft Historic Site. Who’s he? Oh, just one of our presidents.

![Image 25: Cincinnati, OH facts](https://www.cardrates.com/images/uploads/2023/08/Cincinnati-stats.jpg?width=723&height=160)

## 9. Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania

People think of Pittsburgh as a steel town, and for decades that’s what it was. Today it’s a quirky mix of old and new everywhere you look.

For the new, consider a visit to the Andy Warhol Museum. The great pop artist was born in Pittsburgh and brought the rough-hewn city into much of his work. Or visit Randyland, which houses art some may consider pop art’s successor: folk art by Randy Gilson that incorporates construction materials and bits and bobs from here and there.

![Image 26: Pittsburgh, PA](https://www.cardrates.com/images/uploads/2023/08/Skyline-Panorama-of-Pittsburgh.jpg?width=723&height=384)

“[Skyline Panorama of Pittsburgh](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Pittsburgh_skyline_panorama_at_night.jpg)” by Dllu, licensed under [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

Pittsburgh sits at a confluence of rivers, so it also boasts a selection of natural attractions, including Point State Park with its massive fountain, and Schenley Park, where some of the city’s office workers stroll during breaks.

![Image 27: Pittsburgh, PA facts](https://www.cardrates.com/images/uploads/2023/08/Pittsburgh-stats.jpg?width=723&height=160)

## 10. Minneapolis-Saint Paul, Minnesota

Given their urbanity and sophistication, the Twin Cities are surprisingly affordable and stimulating places to visit. There’s culture, such as the Minneapolis Institute of Art, the Cathedral of Saint Paul, and the Basilica of St. Mary.

![Image 28: Minneapolis, MN](https://www.cardrates.com/images/uploads/2023/08/Minneapolis-As-Seen-from-Under-the-Stone-Arch-Bridge.jpg?width=723&height=384)

“[Minneapolis As Seen from Under the Stone Arch Bridge](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Minneapolis_(50433520717).jpg)” by Chad Davis, licensed under [CC BY 2.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0/)

Minneapolis is the birthplace of the great American author F. Scott Fitzgerald of Great Gatsby fame, and you can tour his home there (although you may have to spend a little).

Chain of Lakes is a park for experiencing the area’s aquatic nature. Lake of the Isles provides fantastic walking and biking trails. Lake Harriet is worth a visit if you need a break from asphalt and concrete. And Lebanon Hills Regional Park offers a course in Relaxation 101.

![Image 29: Minneapolis, MN facts](https://www.cardrates.com/images/uploads/2023/08/Minneapolis-stats.jpg?width=723&height=160)

## 11. Norfolk, Virginia

Norfolk is home to Naval Station Norfolk, one of America’s most important military bases. That makes the city a stopping point for military history buffs and anyone interested in America’s defense.

One way to do that is to visit the MacArthur Memorial in Norfolk to commune with the spirit of General Douglas MacArthur, who served honorably in both world wars and beyond as one of America’s great military leaders.

![Image 30: Norfolk, VA](https://www.cardrates.com/images/uploads/2023/08/Skyline-of-Norfolk.jpg?width=723&height=384)

“[Skyline of Norfolk](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Norfolk,_Virginia_skyline_2016.jpg)” by Antony-22, licensed under [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

Or, take in the Armed Forces Memorial down on the Elizabeth River near Town Point Park. There, you’ll reflect on America’s wars and the soldiers and civilians who have fought them to keep us safe.

Norfolk has more than its share of cultural and natural attractions to keep every family member’s attention, so that’s an option too.

![Image 31: Norfolk, VA facts](https://www.cardrates.com/images/uploads/2023/08/Norfolk-stats.jpg?width=723&height=160)

## 12. Rochester, New York

Did someone say Rochester? That’s correct. You may not think much about this town, but it can be a terrific travel destination. Consider that George Eastman of Eastman-Kodak fame headquartered his company there.

![Image 32: Rochester, NY](https://www.cardrates.com/images/uploads/2023/08/High-Falls-in-Downtown-Rochester.jpg?width=723&height=385)

“[High Falls in Downtown Rochester](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Highfallsrochester.jpg)” by Evilarry, licensed under [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)

You can visit Eastman’s boyhood home at the Genesee Country Village and Museum near the city. Or, spend a few dollars and see the George Eastman Museum, where you’ll marvel at the facility’s extensive photography collection and film archives.

Rochester is a working town with parks, historic cemeteries, public markets, and the Erie Canal Trail, which is both a workout and a history class.

![Image 33: Rochester, NY facts](https://www.cardrates.com/images/uploads/2023/08/Rochester-stats.jpg?width=723&height=160)

## 13. Milwaukee, Wisconsin

The Miller Brewery Tour is free. Did we mention the Miller Brewery Tour is free? Up to this point in our survey, we’ve refrained from mentioning that practically every city on this list is a food and beverage paradise and an affordable destination for travel and lodging. We wouldn’t have considered them if they weren’t.

![Image 34: Milwaukee, WI](https://www.cardrates.com/images/uploads/2023/08/Milwaukee-Skyline-2023.jpg?width=723&height=385)

[Milwaukee Skyline 2023](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Milwaukee_Skyline_2023.jpg) by Bfkenney, licensed under [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

But Milwaukee is remarkable in that it’s where German immigrants first brought the crisp, light beer known as lager to the American masses. The Miller Brewery Tour is all about connecting with a city that gave us Miller, Pabst, and Schlitz. And those brands are worth knowing, even if beer is the last thing on your mind.

Check out Milwaukee’s many natural and cultural sites when done with the 80-minute Miller tour. Free samples are available if you’re over 21.

![Image 35: Milwaukee, WI facts](https://www.cardrates.com/images/uploads/2023/08/Milwaukee-stats.jpg?width=723&height=160)

## Methodology

We used Niche’s 2023 list of the [Best Cities to Live in America](https://www.niche.com/places-to-live/search/best-cities/) because it considers many livability factors that are important to travelers. We then filtered the list by low cost of living, walkability, and popularity of restaurants and parks to generate a robust index of traveler-friendly cities.

We used US Bureau of Transportation statistics for average domestic airline itinerary fares by airport for Q1 2023 to rank travel costs. To rank accommodation costs, we used [Booking.com](https://www.booking.com/) to find the average price per night for a weeklong stay at the three cheapest hotels in each city with three- or four-star ratings. [Numbeo](https://www.numbeo.com/cost-of-living/) helped us assess purchasing power, climate, cost of living, and quality of life relative to New York City as a benchmark.

We consulted [TripAdvisor](https://www.tripadvisor.com/) to get a handle on the availability of free activities in each of our cities.

As Americans rebound from pandemic quarantines and shutdowns, many say it’s time to get out there again — and put their words into action. We’re confident our list of underrated travel destinations gives you options that will lead to lasting travel memories.

After enduring long and uncertain pandemic quarantines and shutdowns, Americans have the traveling bug again — in big numbers. A recent [Forbes Advisor Survey](https://www.forbes.com/advisor/credit-cards/inflation-has-not-deflated-americas-travel-plans-2023/) found that 49% of people polled planned on traveling more in 2023 than in 2022. Meanwhile, the popular travel planning site [The Vacationer](https://thevacationer.com/summer-travel-survey-2023/) reported that 85% of Americans surveyed planned at least one trip before Labor Day. It’s a safe bet that travel won’t suddenly fall off the map when cool weather comes.

With vast numbers of people getting on flights and going places, that means extra crowds and cost pressure on many well-known big-city destinations that routinely attract millions.

We evaluated five data points to locate cities that offer lovely travel experiences without breaking the bank. If you’re in the market for a unique adventure but want to save money for everyday expenses, this list of 13 Underrated Travel Destinations to Get the Most Bang for Your Buck is a great way to start. Enjoy the journey!

 Navigate This Article:
